video_title: “We Should’ve Won in ’96” John Smoltz on the Braves Dynasty, Maddux & Glavine + Modern MLB

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the Braves' missed opportunity in the 1996 World Series
quotes.excerpt: When we lost in ’96, at heartbreaking loss, we changed the dynamics of our team forever.
quotes.quote: When we won, it took all the weight in the world off of us. But here’s where it got tough: we should’ve won in ’96. And we would’ve spun a four out of five like the Yankees did, without a doubt. But when we lost in ’96, at heartbreaking loss, we changed the dynamics of our team forever.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the pressure of being a hero in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: In the playoffs, if everyone wants to be the hero, they’re in trouble.
quotes.quote: In the playoffs, if everyone wants to be the hero, they’re in trouble. Everyone gets a little more aggressive, they know it counts more, they know there’s more eyeballs on them. Some people don’t want to be in that spot. I thrived in it. I love pressure.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his durability and pitching in the postseason
quotes.excerpt: I went 14 straight years. Not one time coming to spring training did anyone say, you should probably take it easy.
quotes.quote: I went 14 straight years. Not one time coming to spring training did anyone say, you should probably take it easy. And that was at 34 years old. When you should have Tommy John if you’re going to log that many innings and pitch that many postseasons, if there’s a time to have it, it’s because of that. I wouldn’t have chosen any other era to pitch in than the one I pitched in.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on embracing a new role to win a championship
quotes.excerpt: I had to embrace something that wasn’t my first choice, but if it gave us a chance to win a championship, I’m all in.
quotes.quote: I had to embrace something that wasn’t my first choice, but if it gave us a chance to win a championship, I’m all in. And in three years, amassing 154 saves, which still blows my mind, we didn’t win one series.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on how playing the accordion taught him discipline
quotes.excerpt: I look back and the accordion taught me discipline. It taught me sacrifice, be prepared.
quotes.quote: I look back and the accordion taught me discipline. It taught me sacrifice, be prepared. It’s a hard instrument to play. You just can’t go up there and milly vanilly it. I worked hard at it and I guess I was good, I got some trophies, but I don’t remember.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his childhood dream of becoming a Major League Baseball player
quotes.excerpt: I told my mom at seven years old I was going to be a Major League Baseball player.
quotes.quote: I told my mom at seven years old I was going to be a Major League Baseball player. Where that came from I have no idea, whether it was watching TV. I just felt like that’s what I knew I wanted to be. And again, sports is not in our house. My parents didn’t know anything about sports.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on learning competitiveness from his father
quotes.excerpt: I learned competitiveness through my dad. My dad never let me win at anything, in any game that we ever played.
quotes.quote: I learned competitiveness through my dad. My dad never let me win at anything, in any game that we ever played. And when I turned the tables on him, it was over. And he would just laugh and know that he had no chance to beat me in ping pong or basketball or card games. We were a game playing family.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the importance of believing in your path
quotes.excerpt: If you don’t think it, you won’t believe it. If you don’t believe it, you’ll never dream it.
quotes.quote: I’ve heard it say, if you don’t think it, you won’t believe it. If you don’t believe it, you’ll never dream it. If you don’t dream it, you’re never going to achieve it. And so you’ve got to almost believe this is the path you’re going to be on.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his growth spurt and confidence in high school
quotes.excerpt: I grew seven inches between my sophomore and junior year. The confidence that I had was literally built in that.
quotes.quote: I grew seven inches between my sophomore and junior year. I have a really small mom and small dad, and I’m the tallest guy in like the whole lineage of our families, 6’3”. So I basically was the shortest kid on every team but could throw. They made fun of me till they saw me throw. And I always was a point guard and could handle the ball and couldn’t take it from me. But I grew seven inches between my sophomore and junior year. The confidence that I had was literally built in that.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on playing in Magic Johnson's league
quotes.excerpt: I played in Magic Johnson’s league. That’s where Magic, J. Vincent, Sam Vincent, they all came out of there.
quotes.quote: I played in Magic Johnson’s league. That’s where Magic, J. Vincent, Sam Vincent, they all came out of there. We were a school that was not known for basketball and we did not have any success. And I transferred there in my junior year, we almost, we got to the Elite Eight and we should’ve gotten to the semis. I rolled my ankle with a minute 30 to go and we lost. But that competition, that playing against those guys, really helped me for baseball.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the importance of not showing weakness to opponents
quotes.excerpt: If you convey that you’re the weaker one or that the other person has an advantage, you’re in trouble.
quotes.quote: I’m a big believer that if you convey that you’re the weaker one or that the other person has an advantage, you’re in trouble. So when I stand on the mound and I know the guy at the plate is better than me, I’m never letting him know that. And I’ll fake it. And if I’m playing against guys that are better than me in basketball, I am never going to let them know that they’re better than me.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on being drafted in the 22nd round
quotes.excerpt: I was ticked when I got drafted 22nd round. And part of the reason I got drafted 22nd round is I signed really fast.
quotes.quote: I was ticked when I got drafted 22nd round. And part of the reason I got drafted 22nd round is I signed really fast to go to Michigan State. So the first chance I could get, I knew where I wanted to go and I made one trip to the University of Michigan and I said, heck no, I’m going to Michigan State.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the leverage of being a first-round pick
quotes.excerpt: College to me gives the player leverage to negotiate.
quotes.quote: College to me gives the player leverage to negotiate. First round money back then was $100,000. It’s a lot of money back then, but it’s nowhere close to the 10 and 8 and 7 million that, you know, happened for a long time till they capped it.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his coach Tom Smith's advice
quotes.excerpt: The coach for Michigan State was Tom Smith and he helped me. If you get first round money, you have to go.
quotes.quote: The coach for Michigan State was Tom Smith and he helped me. I don’t know many coaches that would help the only scholarship player, full scholarship player they had ever had was me. And he goes, if you get first round money, you have to go. I don’t know any other coach that would’ve said that. He would’ve wanted to say, no, come to my program and we’ll enhance it and you’ll get more money later.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his difficult first year in Detroit
quotes.excerpt: I was having a miserable year. We were a miserable team. We were 30 games out of first place.
quotes.quote: I was having a miserable year. We were a miserable team. We were 30 games out of first place. We had eight projected Major League Baseball players, prospects on that team. It was just a miserable year and I was having a bad year. And I get the notice that I’m getting traded and I’m just like devastated.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on his philosophy regarding emotions
quotes.excerpt: In life, everything I’ve done, I’ve never acted on an emotion. I let the emotion happen.
quotes.quote: In life, everything I’ve done, I’ve never acted on an emotion. I let the emotion happen and then after 36 hours or 48 hours you go, all right, put your big boy pants on, here we go.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the lack of specialized coaching in the minors
quotes.excerpt: This was so long ago. Detroit had one coach on our team. No pitching coach, no first base coach.
quotes.quote: This was so long ago. Detroit had one coach on our team. No pitching coach, no first base coach, no third base coach. Just one coach, the manager. We had no help. And so I saw a pitching coach twice in the year. So I’m a lost puppy. I don’t know what I’m doing.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on Leo Mazzone's impact on his pitching
quotes.excerpt: Leo Mazzone really helped me. He said, one thing that really changed the dynamic for me. I want you to be an athlete.
quotes.quote: Leo Mazzone really helped me. He said, one thing that really changed the dynamic for me. He said, I want you to be an athlete. Throw a pitch athletically. Detroit changed my entire motion, my entire mechanics. I was as lost as you can be.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the Braves' turnaround from bad to good
quotes.quote: It didn’t always start out that way, right? We all took our lumps. Glavine almost lost 20 games. I was two and seven my first time in the big leagues. We were allowed to go through it. We were allowed to learn from it. We weren’t coddled, we weren’t put handcuffs on us. They said, go. And it served us so well that when we got a better team, we knew we were going to be better. And we knew how to survive. When you’re on a terrible team that loses 100 and guys are like somewhat going through the motions, there’s an opportunity to learn. And when you get, we brought in players that have won that started teaching us. Valuable. They weren’t there very long for the 14, but they taught us and passed the baton on.

quotes.speaker: John Smoltz
quotes.summary_phrase: John Smoltz on the burden of being the best pitcher
quotes.excerpt: I had the burden of I was supposed to be the best pitcher on the staff because I had the best stuff.
quotes.quote: I had the burden of I was supposed to be the best pitcher on the staff because I had the best stuff. Well, that’s a burden when you don’t deliver statistically in the eyes of somebody else when they don’t know what you’re going through. So I had the best stuff, but the best pitchers were Glavine and Maddux. And so where I gained advantage was in the postseason. My stuff could play out in the postseason a little bit more than theirs. But in a regular season, there was nobody better than those two.
